newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's monetary policy to focus on stability.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's monetary policy to focus on stability.

text.p: Central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said on Wednesday Indonesia's monetary policy in 1997 would continue to focus on strengthening macro-economic stability.
"For this purpose, credit growth is set at 17 percent in 1997/98 (April-March) and and this is expected to hold M2 growth down to 18 percent," he told an annual bankers' dinner.

Indonesia's 1997/98 state budget projects broad M-2 money supply to grow by 18 percent to 323.6 trillion rupiah in fiscal 1997/98, while narrow M-1 money was expected to rise by 16 percent to 71.55 trillion rupiah.
The year-on-year M-2 growth last November was 28 percent and M-1 was 19 percent.
"The monetary policy was expected to maintain the level of domestic interest rates capable of maintaining internal and external equilibrium," he said.

"If possible, efforts will also be made to reduce the differential between offshore and domestic interest rates to a reasonable level that does not attract large inflows of a short-term and speculative nature," he said.

Djiwandono said these efforts would curb the monetary expansion generated by capital inflows, particularly from short term funds attracted solely by the relatively high differential between domestic and international interest rates.
"Along with this, the rupiah exchange rate will be maintained at a realistic level without anti-export bias," he said.
He said that the government, to support the efforts in the monetary sector, was also adopting a prudent fiscal policy through the continued pursuit of a balanced, dynamic budget policy.
"As and when needed, the government will not hesistate to apply a fiscal policy that will generate a surplus," he said.
"Without the support of such fiscal policy, the goals of monetary policy will be difficult to achieve," he said.
